body.x: XR content has been evaluated mostly through surveys after the experience and observation. Surveys and observation can record that an experience was uncomfortable, but not where in the experience the problem began or why.

NINEFIVE, which develops digital experiences with web and app technologies, AI and XR, exhibited XR LUMINA at the 57th Korea Electronics Show (KES 2026), held from Oct. 13 to 16 at COEX in Seoul. NINEFIVE is represented by Younghee Jo. XR LUMINA is an integrated XR UX evaluation platform for organizations that create, adopt and operate XR content. At the show, the company aimed to demonstrate data-based validation of XR outcomes and to explore industry-specific pilot and collaboration opportunities.The platform connects web-based test design, data collection during VR, AR and MR experiences, and the review of analysis results and improvement recommendations. It cross-analyzes five models, covering surveys, interaction, posture risk, cybersickness and eye tracking, on a shared experience timeline. These models draw on behavioral, video, physiological and response data.

XR-specific functions include cybersickness estimation using 24 ECG-derived heart-rate variability (HRV) indicators, video-based joint-angle and RULA posture-risk analysis, and gaze heatmaps. The platform also provides evaluation metrics tailored to training, exhibitions, gaming and meditation, a UX indicator report that interprets scores with reference to 84 XR user experience research papers, with citations and sources, and conversational and AI-assisted heuristic reports.

XR LUMINA was jointly developed through industry-academia collaboration among NINEFIVE, Yonsei University, Hanyang University, Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, Kookmin University, Skonec Entertainment and DeepBrain AI. NINEFIVE led platform design and development and interaction analysis. Yonsei University contributed UX metrics, survey frameworks, eye-tracking analysis and heuristic reporting, Hanyang University worked on posture-risk and cybersickness analysis, and Hankuk University of Foreign Studies developed the UX indicator report.
NINEFIVE says its core strength is turning evaluation that relied on simple surveys and observation into improvement evidence based on actual experience data.

For overseas markets, NINEFIVE is looking for cooperation with XR content developers, research institutions and platform and systems integration (SI) companies. Its product brochure lays out seven application areas: construction and plant safety training; manufacturing and equipment education; defense training and simulation; exhibition and retail space experiences; platform and SI integration; device ecosystems; and technology commercialization and field validation. Training applications can assess task success and failure and posture risk, exhibitions can examine gaze heatmaps and experience metrics, and device applications can evaluate cybersickness and presence. On this basis, the company plans to look for joint proofs of concept (PoCs), evaluation-function integration and tailored deployments with international partners.

The company plans to develop XR LUMINA from a tool for reviewing individual test results into a platform for continuous XR quality management, along four lines. It will expand industry-specific metrics and industry-focused AI agents. It will add organization and team accounts, role-based permissions, project histories and before-and-after comparisons to support repeated evaluation. It will extend data collection to wearable data from PPG devices and smartwatches and to EEG analysis models. And it will widen the support of its Unity-based SDK and its connectivity with external systems.

The 57th Korea Electronics Show (KES 2026) ran from Oct. 13 (Tuesday) to 16 (Friday) in Halls A and B at COEX in Seoul. The Korea Electronics Association (KEA) organized the show, and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources hosted it. The KES website lists 500 exhibitors and 1,100 booths. Its themes included electronic parts and materials such as sensors, connectors, printed circuit boards (PCBs) and power supplies; AI transformation (AX) fields such as generative AI, on-device AI, AI chips and smart home and wearable devices; mobility; robotics; digital health; ESG; and Web 3.0 and XR. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event featured X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony took place on Oct. 13.
